parsed.notes: No treatment/currency findings raised. No text/*.txt files were present, so quote and support review used the disclosed lake records and pinpoints only.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Mincey v. Arizona, 437 U.S. 385, U.S. Supreme Court, 1978.
Pinpoint pin-392 supports no murder-scene exception and says seriousness of the offense does not by itself create exigent circumstances.
Lake identity/citation matches Vale v. Louisiana, 399 U.S. 30, U.S. Supreme Court, 1970.
Pinpoints pin-34 and pin-35 support that an outside/front-steps arrest does not justify a warrantless house search or create its own exigency.

defect.evidence_quote: Evidence obtained under a genuinely independent warrant is not tainted by a prior illegal entry.
defect.problem: The independent-source half is supported, but the broad assertion that officers may secure premises pending a warrant is not affirmatively supported by the disclosed Segura record; the disclosed rule addresses evidence later obtained under an independent warrant after a prior illegal entry.
defect.proposed_fix: Use Segura for the independent-source/admissibility point only, or add a disclosed pinpoint supporting lawful temporary securing.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Segura v. United States, 468 U.S. 796, U.S. Supreme Court, 1984.
The only disclosed Segura rule pinpoint supports independent-source admissibility, not the standalone securing rule.
residual_risks: Full opinion text or an additional pinpoint may support the securing clause, but it is not in the disclosed evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Frame as: evidence later seized under a warrant based on wholly independent information is admissible despite the earlier entry.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Lange v. California, 594 U.S. 295, U.S. Supreme Court, 2021.
Pinpoint pin-op1 states there is no categorical rule for pursuit of a fleeing misdemeanor suspect; exigency is judged case by case.
Lake identity/citation matches United States v. Santana, 427 U.S. 38, U.S. Supreme Court, 1976.

Pinpoint pin-43 supports that a suspect may not defeat an arrest set in motion in a public place by retreating to a private place; the lake record also flags Lange as limiting misdemeanor-pursuit readings.

defect.problem: The case exists, but the cited reporter form 607 U.S. ___ is not supported by the lake record; the official/display citation fields are null and final U.S. Reports pagination is pending.
defect.proposed_fix: Cite as Case v. Montana, No. 24-624, slip op. (U.S. Jan. 14, 2026), or omit the U.S. reporter until the official citation appears in the record.

reasons: Lake identity confirms Case v. Montana, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2026-01-14, docket 24-624.
Lake citations.official and citations.display are null; identity.reason_code is recent_or_no_official_cite.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: The substantive aid-standard proposition is supported by pin-slip8 and pin-slip10; only the citation form fails.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches New York v. Harris, 495 U.S. 14, U.S. Supreme Court, 1990.
Pinpoints pin-17, pin-19, and pin-21 support that a Payton violation does not suppress an outside-the-home statement when police had probable cause.
Lake identity/citation matches Illinois v. McArthur, 531 U.S. 326, U.S. Supreme Court, 2001.
Pinpoints pin-331 and pin-334 support a temporary restraint on reentry, supported by probable cause, while police diligently obtain a warrant.
Lake identity/citation matches the Hayden case at 387 U.S. 294, U.S. Supreme Court, 1967, though the canonical lake caption is Warden, Maryland Penitentiary v. Hayden.
Pinpoints pin-298 and pin-299 support warrantless entry in immediate pursuit of an armed robber where delay would endanger lives.
residual_risks: Caption is shortened on the page, but the citation and lake file identify the same case.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the full lake caption if exact canonical naming is required.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Minnesota v. Carter, 525 U.S. 83, U.S. Supreme Court, 1998.
Pinpoint pin-90 supports that a temporary commercial visitor present only a few hours has no reasonable expectation of privacy in the host home.
Lake identity/citation matches Caniglia v. Strom, 593 U.S. 194, U.S. Supreme Court, 2021.
Pinpoints pin-op3 and pin-op4 support that Cady's community-caretaking rationale does not create a freestanding home-entry exception.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For the warrant/exigency/emergency-aid list, cross-cite the supporting home-entry cases if this sentence is used outside this page.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Maryland v. Buie, 494 U.S. 325, U.S. Supreme Court, 1990.
Pinpoints pin-334 and pin-335 support the two-tier protective-sweep rule: adjacent spaces without suspicion and broader sweeps on articulable danger facts.

defect.evidence_quote: Absent exigent circumstances, that threshold may not reasonably be crossed without a warrant.
defect.problem: Citation/existence match and the warrantless-entry firm-line rule is supported, but the disclosed Payton record does not verify the second proposition that an arrest warrant plus reason to believe the suspect is within authorizes entry into the suspect's own home.
defect.proposed_fix: Add a disclosed Payton pinpoint for the arrest-warrant/residence/presence passage or narrow the row to the supported warrantless-entry rule.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Payton v. New York, 445 U.S. 573, U.S. Supreme Court, 1980.
The disclosed Payton pinpoints are pin-576 and pin-590; they support the firm-line warrant requirement, not the arrest-warrant-plus-presence authority.
residual_risks: A full opinion text or missing Payton pinpoint may verify the second clause, but it is not disclosed here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split Payton into two supported propositions and add the missing pinpoint for the arrest-warrant authority.

defect.evidence_quote: The test keys on whether the police acted lawfully before the exigency arose:
defect.problem: The disclosed King pinpoint supports a lawful-before-exigency test, but it does not itself substantiate the exact 'only conduct that itself violates or threatens the Fourth Amendment' formulation.
defect.proposed_fix: Tighten to the disclosed formulation or add the exact King passage for the 'violates or threatens' language.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Kentucky v. King, 563 U.S. 452, U.S. Supreme Court, 2011.
The narrower police-created-exigency proposition is supported by the disclosed rule summary.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Say: police-created exigency turns on whether police acted lawfully before the exigency arose.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Brigham City v. Stuart, 547 U.S. 398, U.S. Supreme Court, 2006.
Pinpoints pin-400 and pin-404 support warrantless emergency-aid entry judged objectively, without regard to the officer's subjective arrest motivation.
Lake identity/citation matches Sabbath v. United States, 391 U.S. 585, U.S. Supreme Court, 1968.
The lake record supports the unannounced breaking point, including opening a closed but unlocked door, and pinpoints tie it to the announcement requirement.
Lake identity/citation matches Minnesota v. Olson, 495 U.S. 91, U.S. Supreme Court, 1990.
Pinpoint pin-98 supports that an overnight guest has a reasonable expectation of privacy in the host's home sufficient to challenge a warrantless entry.
Lake identity/citation matches Steagald v. United States, 451 U.S. 204, U.S. Supreme Court, 1981.
Pinpoint pin-205 supports that an arrest warrant for one person does not authorize searching a third party's home without consent or exigent circumstances.
Lake identity/citation matches Kirk v. Louisiana, 536 U.S. 635, U.S. Supreme Court, 2002, per curiam.
Pinpoint pin-638 directly supports that police need either a warrant or probable cause plus exigent circumstances to enter a home lawfully.

defect.evidence_quote: The seriousness of the crime bears directly on whether an exigency justifies a warrantless home entry
defect.problem: The quoted 'rarely be sanctioned' point is supported, but 'caps exigency' is stronger than the disclosed rule, which says offense seriousness bears directly on the exigency analysis.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace 'caps exigency' with 'bears directly on' or 'strongly limits' exigency.

reasons: Lake identity/citation matches Welsh v. Wisconsin, 466 U.S. 740, U.S. Supreme Court, 1984.
Pinpoint pin-755 supports that home-entry exigency for a minor offense should rarely be sanctioned.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the lake's 'bears directly on' formulation to avoid a categorical-sounding overclaim.

defect.evidence_quote: In terms that apply equally to seizures of property and to seizures of persons, the Fourth Amendment has drawn a firm line at the entrance to the house. Absent exigent circumstances, that threshold may not reasonably be crossed without a warrant.
defect.problem: The Payton firm-line quote, Steagald third-party rule, and Kirk probable-cause-plus-exigency point are supported, but the disclosed record does not verify the sentence that an arrest warrant carries limited authority to enter the arrestee's own home when there is reason to believe he is within. No Payton pinpoint for that passage and no full opinion text are disclosed.
defect.proposed_fix: Add a disclosed Payton pinpoint for the arrest-warrant/residence/presence rule, or remove that sentence from the black-letter rule before seeking black-letter approvals.

reasons: Payton pin-590 verifies the firm-line quote and pincite.
Steagald pin-205 and Kirk pin-638 support adjacent pieces, but not the missing Payton arrest-warrant authority.
residual_risks: A missing Payton pinpoint may cure the defect; it is not in the disclosed evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Separate the supported warrantless-entry rule from the arrest-warrant entry authority and cite each with its own pinpoint.

defect.problem: The assertion is only a transclusion of Entry to Arrest; the target source or rendered transcluded rule is not in the disclosed files, so the black-letter content cannot be reviewed for support, quote fidelity, or pincite accuracy.
defect.proposed_fix: Provide the target Entry to Arrest source file or include the rendered black-letter text in content_page.md/group_inventory.
